summary: Apple's Automator is a workflow engine that runs ordered action bundles and shell or AppleScript actions, with a workflow view and controller. BifrOSt has no workflow engine and no loadable action bundles. Its closest parts are the Shortcuts app, which stores and edits ordered lists of built-in actions, and the App Intents SDK, which gives apps typed actions. Shortcuts runs nothing yet: its actions are only logged because the shell cannot receive them over the app protocol.

features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 32 tests. Apps declare typed intents in code and manifest.toml [[intent]] tables and serve them over the control socket. There is no bundle format, no install location scan (Automator loads /System/Library/Automator, /Library/Automator, ~/Library/Automator) and no view for action parameters.

verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Wave 1 (parity/integration 0d0412c3): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No SDK API runs a shell script as a workflow step. The control socket (springboard/sdk/src/control.rs) is for calling apps, not for scripted steps.

features.apple: AMWorkflow (actions, addAction, insertAction, moveAction, removeAction, input, output, valueForVariable)
features.bifrost: springboard/apps/shortcuts-desktop/src/model.rs (Shortcut { name, color, actions }, Action enum, parse/serialise one line per shortcut)
features.note: Shortcuts stores an ordered list of up to 24 built-in actions per shortcut, capped at 64 shortcuts. It has no variables, no input or output passing between steps, and no workflow file format beyond shortcuts.tsv in the app data directory.

verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Wave 1 (parity/integration 0d0412c3): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. run_all only queues actions into a list and shows a toast. main.rs logs them as unavailable. Nothing executes Wi-Fi, Do Not Disturb, brightness, screenshot, timer or open-app actions, and there is no pause, step or stop.

features.bifrost: springboard/apps/shortcuts-desktop/src/widget.rs (View::Editor, the Add Action list driven by model.rs KINDS)
features.note: The editor adds, removes and reorders built-in actions. It cannot edit action parameters through a generic view and cannot be embedded by other apps.

features.apple: AMAction offering actions to workflows; Shortcuts listing actions from installed apps
features.note: The shell lists shortcut = true intents in Spotlight and runs parameterless ones. The Shortcuts app does not yet list or run intents from other apps (documented gap in docs/bifrost-ui.md around line 978).

verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 32 tests. Intent calls return JSON-RPC errors. There is no workflow-level error domain and no way to stop a multi-step run on a failed step, because multi-step runs do not exist.
Apple marks this class deprecated and it depends on OSA scripting. BifrOSt has no AppleScript runtime and does not plan one.

gaps: No workflow engine: multi-step runs, variables and input/output passing between actions do not exist.
Shortcuts actions that need the shell (Wi-Fi, Low Power, Do Not Disturb, brightness, open app, screenshot, timer) are logged, not executed (springboard/apps/shortcuts-desktop/src/main.rs).
No action bundle format or install scan: no equivalent of /System/Library/Automator, /Library/Automator or ~/Library/Automator.
No workflow controller (run, pause, step, stop, reset) and no runWorkflow-by-path API.
Shortcuts does not list or run intents from other installed apps yet (docs/bifrost-ui.md, App Intents gaps).
No shell script action API for workflow steps.
